newsitem.title: FINLAND: FINNISH EMU VOTE DUE EARLY IN 1998 -PM LIPPONEN.
newsitem.headline: FINNISH EMU VOTE DUE EARLY IN 1998 -PM LIPPONEN.

text.p: Prime Minister Paavo Lipponen said on Thursday that parliament would vote early next year for or against Finnish membership of EMU.

After a meeting with parliamentary group leaders from the five government as well as opposition parties, Lipponen told reporters there was now political consensus that parliament should not vote on EMU in connection with a debate this spring on a government report on the single currency.
The political leaders had agreed that "no decision on Finland's participation in the third stage of EMU will be made (in connection with the spring debate)," he said.
"The vote will come at the earliest in the beginning of 1998," Lipponen said.

The government will present a report outlining potential pros and cons of EMU membership in spring, and Lipponen said parliament leaders had agreed to bring the debate to a close before the legislature's summer recess.

The left-right-green coalition has stated as its target that Finland will meet this year all entry criteria for the single currency, so parliament will have a real choice between joining or remaining outside the single currency.
